questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In the laboratory, in aqueous solution, why are secondary amines often more basic than primary amines?

options.text: Secondary amines have fewer hydrogens to lose
options.misconception: basicity concerns proton acceptance, not loss

options.text: Alkyl groups donate electron density and solvation differences balance
Primary amines are always more basic
options.misconception: solvation can favor primary in some cases

questions.explanation: Alkyl groups donate electron density to nitrogen, increasing basicity from primary to secondary, but solvation of the ammonium ion becomes less favorable as substitution increases, so secondary amines often show the highest aqueous basicity.
questions.hint: Induction raises basicity while solvation can lower it.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In the laboratory, which sequence converts a ketone into an amine with one additional carbon-nitrogen bond?

options.text: Formation of an oxime then hydrolysis
options.misconception: that gives a ketone or aldehyde

options.text: Condensation with an amine followed by reduction

questions.explanation: Reductive amination condenses a carbonyl with ammonia or an amine to an imine or iminium ion, which is then reduced in situ by a mild hydride donor to give the amine with a new carbon-nitrogen bond.
questions.hint: Imine formation then reduction.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In the laboratory, what class of amine is prepared cleanly by the Gabriel synthesis?

options.misconception: arylation does not work in Gabriel

questions.explanation: Gabriel synthesis uses phthalimide anion to alkylate once and then releases the amine by hydrolysis or hydrazinolysis, giving a primary alkylamine without the overalkylation problems of direct ammonia alkylation.
questions.hint: Gabriel gives primary alkylamines.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In the laboratory, treating benzenediazonium chloride with copper(I) bromide gives which product?
questions.explanation: A copper(I) bromide Sandmeyer reaction replaces the diazonium group with bromine, releasing nitrogen gas and forming bromobenzene through a copper-mediated radical pathway.
questions.hint: Copper bromide gives aryl bromide.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In the laboratory, what alkene is the major product of Hofmann elimination of an unsymmetrical quaternary ammonium hydroxide?
questions.explanation: Hofmann elimination of a quaternary ammonium hydroxide proceeds by E2 with a bulky leaving group, giving predominantly the less substituted alkene because removal of the more accessible beta hydrogen is favored sterically.
questions.hint: Hofmann rule favors the less substituted alkene.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In the laboratory, which reagent converts an amine into an amide most readily?
questions.explanation: Acid chlorides react rapidly with amines by nucleophilic acyl substitution to give amides, whereas carboxylic acids first form ammonium salts and require coupling agents or activation.
questions.hint: Acid chlorides acylate amines readily.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In the laboratory, why is aniline much less basic than cyclohexylamine?

options.text: Aniline has a larger molar mass
Aniline is more soluble in water
The ring withdraws by induction only
options.misconception: resonance delocalization is the main cause

options.text: The nitrogen lone pair is delocalized into the aromatic ring

questions.explanation: In aniline the nitrogen lone pair overlaps with the aromatic pi system and is delocalized into the ring, making it less available to bind a proton, whereas in cyclohexylamine the lone pair is localized on nitrogen.
questions.hint: Resonance delocalization lowers basicity.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In the laboratory, why is direct alkylation of ammonia with an alkyl halide often inefficient for making a primary amine?

options.text: The primary amine product is itself nucleophilic and reacts further
Alkyl halides do not react with amines

questions.explanation: The primary amine formed is more nucleophilic than ammonia and reacts again with alkyl halide, leading to mixtures of secondary, tertiary and quaternary products, which is why protected routes such as Gabriel synthesis are preferred.
questions.hint: Product overreacts with the alkyl halide.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In the laboratory, what happens when an amine is treated with aqueous hydrochloric acid?

options.text: It forms a water-soluble ammonium salt

options.misconception: the salt is more water soluble

questions.explanation: An amine is protonated by hydrochloric acid to give an ammonium chloride salt, which is ionic and therefore much more water soluble than the neutral amine.
questions.hint: Protonation gives a soluble ammonium salt.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In the laboratory, what product forms when a nitrile is reduced with lithium aluminum hydride?

options.misconception: hydrolysis, not reduction, gives an acid

questions.explanation: Lithium aluminum hydride reduces the carbon-nitrogen triple bond of a nitrile all the way to a primary amine, adding two hydrogens to the carbon and two to the nitrogen.
questions.hint: Nitrile reduction gives a primary amine.
